title: create-github-app-token repositories takes bare repo names, not owner/repo
answers: GitHub App token has no access to repository after scoping
why not use github.repository for create-github-app-token repositories
scoped app token matches no repository
body:
Symptom: after adding repository scope to a GitHub App token step, the issued token matches no repository.
Root cause: the `repositories` input of actions/create-github-app-token takes bare repository names; `${{ github.repository }}` expands to `owner/name` (e.g. `mlflow/mlflow`), which matches nothing.
Fix pattern: write literal bare names alongside `owner`, e.g. `owner: mlflow` and `repositories: mlflow`; for several repos use a comma-separated literal such as `repositories: mlflow,internal` as in .github/workflows/nailaopus.yml.
Constraints: do not derive `repositories` from `github.repository` or other expressions that include the owner prefix; the policy rule only checks that the value is non-empty, so a wrong format passes conftest.
applies: Writing or editing with.repositories for actions/create-github-app-token in workflow YAML.
says: A scoped GitHub App token has no access to repositories after restricting permissions.
Automation steps fail with permission errors because the generated application token matches no repository.
Why does my scoped application token have access to zero repositories during workflow execution?
Allow the workflow bot token to access designated repositories without permission denied failures.
Restricting application token access to specific repositories resulted in an invalid empty scope.
search: The repositories input of actions/create-github-app-token requires literal bare repository names rather than owner-prefixed expressions such as ${{ github.repository }}. Passing owner/name causes the issued token to match no repository, whereas bare names such as owner: mlflow with repositories: mlflow or comma-separated lists correctly grant scope. The policy rule in .github/policy.rego only checks that the input is non-empty, allowing improperly formatted names to pass conftest.
